name: Ismachiah
overview: Ismachiah was a male Levite who served as the overseer of the consecrated things under Conaniah, indicating a role of responsibility in the sacred service of the temple. His position highlights his trusted status within the Levitical order during the time recorded in 2 Chronicles 31:13. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Ismachiah means 'Yahweh sustains,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning tied to God's sustaining power. This proper name is noted in 2 Chronicles 31:13 and emphasizes the divine support behind his service.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Ismachiah as a descendant of Levi, situating him within the Levitical tribe known for temple duties. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ismachiah's role as overseer of the consecrated things under Conaniah places him in a critical position of stewardship over sacred temple items, reflecting faithful administration in the worship life of Israel. His service during the reforms recorded in 2 Chronicles 31 underscores the restoration and proper management of temple worship under King Hezekiah's reign. Thus, Ismachiah represents faithful Levitical service aligned with God's covenantal worship.
